correctness.rationale: For any finite interval, the Skorokhod balance gives |(R-U)-A|<=L exactly; the stationary two-state tilted generator has dominant eigenvalue -lambda+sqrt(lambda²+v²q²), independent Brownian noise adds Dq², and bounded perturbation transfers the LDP. For D>0 the derivative is steep and strictly increasing. For D=0 the interior Legendre transform is explicit and no-flip events establish endpoint lower bounds. The positive optimizer near j=v scales as (lambda²/(vD))^(1/3); uniform large-q expansion proves the stated 1/3 height and 2/3 width profile. A standalone standard-library checker passed 1607 numerical, algebraic and pathwise consistency tests. Limits are sequential and no finite testing is used as proof.

originality.rationale: The actual novelty scope is the thermal D>0 signed-wall large-deviation function and its fractional-power rounding of the athermal ballistic support edge. Previously derived athermal wall covariance and Bressloff’s joint athermal occupation transform are explicitly treated as prior, not claimed new. General reflected-process LDP methods are also prior. Searches and full-text checks did not find an explicit mixed-thermal signed-wall edge with these coefficients; priority remains qualified, not independently certified.
residual_risks: A general result on colored-noise reflection LDP may imply the bounded-coboundary SCGF equivalence, a standard technique; novelty is limited to the motivated singular telegraph thermal edge profile.
The full athermal occupation-time transform of Bressloff has implicit coverage of athermal results.
An unlocated explicit singular small-noise edge theorem for the same tilted telegraph-plus-Brownian current would supersede this result; no independent publication-priority audit has occurred.

value.rationale: Mean active pressure and Gaussian wall-noise variance do not predict a rare fluctuation tail outside the athermal ballistic support. The exact D^(1/3) loss of boundary rate and D^(2/3) current scale classify how arbitrarily weak thermal translation opens new force-imbalance tails, with a finite-box geometry-independent observable and a computable universal crossover. This is a physically motivated boundary singularity, not an arbitrary small numerical correction or unmotivated slice.
